Forecasts from a calendar variation model

Source: R/forecast.R
forecast.lunarcast.Rd

Future calendar regressors are built from the holiday dates. For a two-level effect, the effect of every new occurrence comes from the level-2 rule and its uncertainty (the one-step-ahead CV error of that rule, growing linearly with the occurrence index) is added to the ARIMA forecast variance.

Usage

# S3 method for lunarcast
forecast(object, h = 2 * frequency(object$y), level = 95, level2 = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

A `lunarcast` object.

h

Forecast horizon (periods).

level

Confidence level (a single value, in percent).

level2

Optional override of the level-2 rule: a method name or a fixed log effect (scenario), e.g. `list(adha = log(2.5))`.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class `"forecast"`. With `lambda = 0` the point forecast is the median. New occurrence effects are in `$future_effects`.

Examples

fit <- lunarcast(sapi, list(adha = holiday_dates("idul_adha")),
                 window = c(-3, 7), effect = "two-level",
                 trend = "stochastic", season = "none")
fc <- forecast(fit, h = 12)
fc$future_effects
#> $adha
#>        event     alpha        se method    ratio
#> 1 2026-05-27 0.9513161 0.1097002  wmean 2.589115
#> 
# scenario: the next Eid al-Adha doubles the level
forecast(fit, h = 12, level2 = list(adha = log(2)))$mean
#>           Jan      Feb      Mar      Apr      May      Jun      Jul      Aug
#> 2025                                                                        
#> 2026 21.50183 21.60499 21.40378 21.28097 36.53332 26.83049 21.04526 21.07882
#>           Sep      Oct      Nov      Dec
#> 2025                            20.88173
#> 2026 21.10937 21.14123 21.14944
